1. BUILD, CHOOSE A COIN AND POOL
Enter from the workroom, put a rig in an unlocked rack slot and install intact GPUs. Choose a coin and pool in room management. Start in Standard mode; check VRAM requirements and tonight's executable plan.

2. KEEP POWER MONEY, THEN SLEEP
Check tonight's plan and retain cash before sleeping. Review credited output and costs next day. Tomorrow's sales cannot pay tonight's power. Reduce running machines when capacity or cash is short.

3. SELL FOR CASH; STOP FOR SERVICING
Preview a coin sale before confirming. Keep money for future power and servicing. Stop low-maintenance rigs before servicing. Try auto-selling, overclock or server leases once familiar with the cycle.

CHECK ACTUAL PARTS FIRST
Open Rig Management, Operating Details and Algorithm Details to inspect each GPU's core tier, actual VRAM and exclusion reason. Rigs include support equipment and take only GPUs. Mixed GPUs are allowed; VRAM is never shared between cards.

THREE ALGORITHMS
Anchor and Singularity use Core: at least 4GB per GPU; extra VRAM adds no speed.
Matrix and Pulse use Memory Bandwidth: at least 8GB, full capability at 16GB.
Stellar uses Large VRAM: at least 16GB, full capability at 32GB.

Broken or undersized GPUs contribute no work and incur no GPU power cost. No eligible GPU means the rig stops.

COMPARE NET OUTPUT AND COMPETITION
Output depends on effective hash rate and current difficulty. Network competition gradually changes difficulty. Compare output, coin price and power cost together: a high price does not guarantee higher profit. Displayed output already deducts mode rejection losses and pool fees.

POOL CHANGES APPLY NEXT DAY
Steady Pool deducts 2% of output. Variable Pool deducts 0.5%, with a 0.70-1.30 luck factor shared by the same coin on the same day. Coins arrive automatically after the next day's settlement; unsettled output cannot be sold.

Balances and tiny output remainders survive coin changes.

CHECK TONIGHT'S PLAN AND STOP REASONS
Power includes device wattage plus 15% shared cooling overhead; cooling counts device heat only. Upgrade power and cooling separately. Both upgrades are needed to unlock the corresponding slots and case tiers.

Active leases reserve capacity first. Rigs are scheduled by priority, then slot number. Machines that cannot fit or cannot be paid for are skipped.

The shop's nightly costs are paid first; remaining cash schedules rigs. Tomorrow's coin sales cannot fund tonight. Stopped rigs pay no rig power and suffer no wear.

STOP, THEN SERVICE
Eco/Standard/Overclock wear is 0.6/1/2 per operating day. Below 60 warns; below 30 disables overclock and adds 3 percentage points of rejection. Zero triggers protective shutdown.

T1-T5 servicing uses 1/1/2/2/3 Electronic Parts and 5/8/12/18/25C. All costs are taken at once to restore maintenance to 100. Materials come from workroom and storage; shortages cancel it. Moving a rig or changing GPUs does not reset maintenance. Servicing does not repair broken parts.

CASH UPFRONT, SERVICE OVER TIME
Servers use CPUs and RAM; actual parts determine capacity. Choose 3/5/7-day leases with 0%/3%/5% bonuses. Signing locks configuration, reserves capacity and prepays the full term's power at the signing-day rate. Net cash rounds down for the whole lease. Power is not charged again during the term. Equipment cannot be removed or changed before expiry.

CASH RECEIVED IS NOT ALL EARNED
Prepaid cash can fund operations, but rent for future service remains unearned. The ledger recognizes rent by service day and lists prepaid power and whole-order rounding separately. A seven-day advance is not first-day net profit.

PREVIEW BEFORE CONFIRMING
Reference quotes are valuation guides. Execution depends on today's depth and cumulative net buys/sells; splitting orders does not remove slippage. Each side pays 1%. Whole cash totals round up for buying, down for selling. A sale netting less than 1C is rejected; keep accumulating.

NORMAL INPUT: 0.0001 COIN
Wallets retain units of 0.000001 coin. Normal inputs use 0.0001-coin steps; Sell All handles wallet remainders. A manual order beyond depth must be resized and confirmed again; it never silently executes part of the order.

After settlement, quote or asset changes, use a fresh preview. Reference market value is not immediately cashable net proceeds.

Chart B/S markers total each day's buys and sells, including auto-sells. Their tooltip price is the daily reference, not the execution price.

Cover Operations follows your coin order toward the next three nights' known power budget. Fixed Share caps the sale at 0%-100% of this night's new output, in 10% steps. Full execution is not guaranteed.

MINIMUM NET PRICE AND LEFTOVERS
The price floor uses whole-order net average after fees, slippage and cash rounding. Below-floor sales are skipped. Automatic sales run at the new day's quote after costs are paid and production is credited. Limited depth may fill part; unsold coins stay in the wallet.

Check next day's report for unsold reasons. Expected sale proceeds are not cash already available.

SEPARATE CASH, PRODUCTION AND HOLDINGS
The ledger retains 90 days. Cash flow records actual trades, operating/servicing costs, expansion and prepaid rent. Production records coins, pool fees and running costs. Reference holdings value and unrealized profit/loss change with prices; unsold coins are not realized cash income.

COUNT EQUIPMENT AND MATERIAL COSTS TOO
Purchased-coin cost includes fees and uses a weighted average. Mined coins have no purchase cost; power is listed separately. Sale quantities are attributed between mined and purchased coins in proportion to wallet holdings.

To calculate total returns, also include actual hardware purchase, repair and servicing-material spending. These costs are not fully tracked here, so ledger returns alone do not establish total profit or an exact payback date.
